question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Ports and geographical locations related to Captain William Hawkins' voyage to India in 1607–1608]
options: Surat — The port where Captain Hawkins anchored the EIC ship Hector in August 1608
London — The departure port of the Third Voyage of the EIC under Hawkins and Keeling
Aden — A port where the EIC ship Hector stopped and Hawkins engaged in trade negotiations before proceeding to India
Calicut — The city where Captain Hawkins landed and established the EIC's first permanent factory in 1608
wrong_fact: Captain Hawkins did NOT land or establish a factory at Calicut in 1608. He landed at Surat, on the western coast of India (Gujarat), and traveled to Agra to meet Jahangir. The EIC's first factory attempt was at Surat, not Calicut.
explanation: Captain William Hawkins commanded the ship Hector during the EIC's Third Voyage. The fleet departed from England (London/Tilbury) in 1607, made stops including Aden, and arrived at Surat on August 24, 1608. Calicut was the primary landing site for the Portuguese (Vasco da Gama in 1498), not Hawkins.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Important coastal and inland cities on Captain Hawkins' route and initial operations in India]
options: Agra — The Mughal imperial capital where Hawkins travelled to present his credentials to Emperor Jahangir
Surat — The estuary of the Tapti River where Hawkins' ship Hector faced armed opposition from Portuguese frigates
Goa — The seat of the Portuguese Viceroy where Hawkins was imprisoned and held for two years before reaching the Mughal court
Daman — A Portuguese coastal stronghold near Surat from which Portuguese naval forces harassed English shipping
wrong_fact: Captain Hawkins was NOT imprisoned or held in Goa for two years. Although the Portuguese at Surat seized some of his men and goods, and threatened him, Hawkins himself avoided Goa and traveled directly from Surat to Agra to meet Emperor Jahangir.
explanation: Upon reaching Surat in August 1608, Hawkins encountered severe Portuguese hostility, as they claimed a monopoly over the port. Despite Portuguese attempts to seize his cargo and ship, Hawkins negotiated with local authorities and made his way inland to Agra. He was never imprisoned in Goa.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical locations along the voyage of the Hector under Captain William Hawkins (1607–1608)]
options: Socotra — An island near the Horn of Africa where Hawkins' companion ship, the Consent, separated from the Hector
Bantam — The ultimate East Indies destination that Hawkins' ship Hector sailed to under William Keeling after Hawkins landed at Surat
Sierra Leone — An Atlantic coastal stopover where the EIC fleet halted to refresh supplies and crew health
Masulipatnam — The port on the Coromandel coast where Hawkins first sighted land in India before sailing around to Surat
wrong_fact: Hawkins did NOT sight land at Masulipatnam or visit the Coromandel coast on his way to Surat. The ship Hector sailed directly across the Indian Ocean from Socotra/Aden to Surat on the western coast of India.
explanation: The Third Voyage of the EIC (consisting of the Hector, Dragon, and Consent) sailed via the Atlantic, stopping at Sierra Leone, rounding the Cape, stopping at Socotra and Aden. From Aden, Hawkins sailed the Hector straight to Surat. Masulipatnam on the eastern coast was visited later by the Globe during the EIC's Seventh Voyage (1611).
